title: Getting Started with Venture Capital in Strawberry
description: Use Strawberry across market intelligence, deal flow, investment decisions, introductions, and portfolio monitoring.

navigation.title: Venture Capital & Investing
navigation.tagline: Markets, deal flow, decisions, and portfolio support

introduction: Venture work moves between market research, company websites, founder conversations, the CRM, internal notes, data rooms, and the firm's own investment history. A useful AI companion needs to work across those surfaces without flattening the judgment into a generic score.

Strawberry brings that work into one visible browser workspace. It can inspect current sources and logged-in tools, carry the firm's accepted thesis and feedback into the next step, and keep consequential actions such as introductions, CRM changes, and sharing separately reviewable.

rows: Map markets and startup ecosystems, follow capital and talent, and understand how relevant investors are deploying capital.
Source companies, research and qualify opportunities, find credible network paths, and keep the pipeline current.
Prepare for founder conversations, test material questions, and build a traceable investment memo.
Notice material company changes, prepare updates, follow commitments, and make useful introductions.

items.context: Start with the investment work and context already in front of you, then choose the most useful workflow.

blocks.text: You do not need to configure the whole system first. One company, market question, upcoming meeting, pipeline review, or portfolio update is enough to begin.

sections.title: Use the investment funnel without forcing it

blocks.text: Deal work often has a recognizable progression. Keeping the handoffs clear prevents early research from pretending to be diligence and prevents a polished memo from hiding missing evidence.

items: Source a thesis-matched set of companies and review a varied sample before widening the search.
Research one opportunity and decide whether the evidence justifies more attention.
Prepare for the founder conversation and preserve what actually changed afterward.
Test the material underwriting questions with appropriately deep diligence.
Write the investment case, counterevidence, risks, and open questions into a decision record.

items.context: Turn the firm's thesis into a calibrated, sourced set of companies worth reviewing.
Build a concise company view with preliminary thesis fit, tensions, and next questions.
Test the claims and risks that could change the investment decision.
Turn accepted research and diligence into a source-linked decision record.

blocks.text: This sequence is useful when the work follows it. An investor preparing for a meeting, reviewing a pipeline, or monitoring a portfolio company can enter elsewhere without retracing every step.

sections.title: Build a view of the market

blocks.text: A startup map should explain the market, not merely return company names. Strawberry can follow current company pages, funding announcements, investor portfolios, accelerator cohorts, databases available in the logged-in browser, hiring, and news while keeping source dates beside the findings.

That makes it possible to compare what investors say they focus on with where they have actually invested, see clusters and white space, and connect the landscape back to the firm's own thesis and pass history.

items.context: Map startups, investors, accelerators, investment activity, and relationships around an investment question.
Use the broader market workflow when category boundaries, value chains, experts, or established companies matter more than startup formation.

sections.title: Keep deal flow grounded in current context

blocks.text: A pipeline field is only one part of the record. A recent founder email, partner note, meeting transcript, or diligence finding may have changed the real status. Strawberry can compare those sources with the current CRM and show the conflict instead of silently choosing one.

The review should tell the team which opportunities deserve attention, where evidence or ownership is missing, and what decision comes next. Proposed CRM changes remain separate until their records, fields, and scope are approved.

items.context: Review active opportunities using the firm's actual stages, decision rules, and recent context.
Apply separately approved investment-record changes using the team's real CRM schema.

sections.title: Treat meetings and introductions as real work

blocks.text: Founder calls, expert conversations, partner meetings, and introductions sit between research and action. Strawberry can prepare from the calendar and relevant relationship context, preserve a reliable meeting record, and carry supported evidence and commitments forward without making the investor reconstruct them.

A warm path needs extra care. A shared contact or old email is evidence to inspect, not proof that someone is close or willing to introduce. The companion can verify the path, explain its freshness, and prepare a considerate ask or double-opt-in introduction while keeping private deal context and sending under the user's control.

items.context: Prepare for a founder, partner, expert, board, or portfolio conversation.
Turn the reliable record into evidence, commitments, questions, and reviewed follow-through.
Find a credible network path and prepare the appropriate introduction or intermediary ask.

sections.title: Support the portfolio without creating noise

blocks.text: Portfolio monitoring is useful when it begins with an agreed materiality bar. A financing, leadership change, product launch, customer signal, regulatory issue, or market shift may matter; repeated coverage of the same announcement usually does not.

Start with one review. Once the investor has corrected the sources and signal rules, a Routine can check the agreed companies and prepare a digest only when something meaningful changes. Current company context can then support a board brief, firm update, or useful introduction.

items.context: Review material company changes against an accepted baseline and monitoring bar.
Turn accepted company or portfolio context into a concise update for the right audience.

sections.title: Teach the companion how the firm invests

blocks.text: The firm's edge is not a generic checklist. It is the accumulated judgment in its thesis, trusted sources, pass reasons, questions, memo structure, and interpretation of evidence. Correct a real result, then let the companion carry the accepted choices into later work.

When a method proves repeatable, save it as a firm skill or share it with the team. Use a Routine only when the trigger, systems, output, destination, approval behavior, and stop conditions are clear. Investment decisions, introductions, sensitive access, CRM changes, and external sharing remain separately controlled.
